# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 21:58 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 247 active entries of tips_notebook.json (46 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

The only real risk is if my Seer read is wrong and Erin is actually Good, with Frank or Grace being the real liars, but my confidence in the "not Good" reading is reasonably strong.

Heidi's "Not Evil" read on Erin rules out Jester or Executioner, pointing instead toward Serial Killer, Arsonist, straightforward Good, or a Yakuza member holding the Katana. I'm also puzzling over whether Niaj could actually be Yakuza despite the Katana death typically signaling a Good victim, and reconsidering Frank's claim about a "confirmed N5 Oracle hit" on Niaj, which seems like an odd detail worth double-checking alongside Erin's voting history against Judy, Dave, and Carol.

Consider a short reminder in the Night phase prompt of which Katana-holder and visit rules apply that night, since the Katana/Ex-Con/swap rules interact.

answers.confusing_rules: The Smuggler's swap tokens and the Katana's 'holder moves' interact confusingly with the R23 swap rules; the claim that a swap 'can't beat Standard protection' was hard to verify. The Medic protection on a non-attacked player is not reported to anyone, so it was unclear whether a Katana 'survived' result implies protection. The R19 exception that the Katana holder reads Good (so Sheriff reads Not Evil) was easy to forget and mattered for trial reasoning. The Cartographer's sizes-only result plus the 'names only with a token' rule was hard to reason about.
answers.missing_information: The Yakuza night-chat summaries gave only actions, not who was role-blocked or whether a Katana attack was blocked, which made it hard to know whether a missing result came from a block. I could not tell from public info which players were visited by whom beyond group sizes. Vote totals were announced without the nominator names in a usable way, so tracking who pushed which trial was manual. I had no way to see whether the Puppeteer's puppet token had been used on a specific day.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As the Smuggler I wanted to use my two swap tokens to redirect a Katana attack away from a protected target or to swap Heidi's Sheriff visit onto a teammate, but the moderator-facing options only let me choose 'no swap' in practice and I did not find a clear way to reason about a swap that would change a Katana outcome. I also wanted to post a private message to a teammate without it being visible, but private messages are visible as to sender and recipient, which I found awkward for coordinating.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Night 2 Yakuza report said Judy 'used no Ritualist action' while the Night 2 Ritualist-related slip ('Ritualist') appeared in public text from Judy, which the moderator treated as a slip; this was not a rule issue but made the public record messy. The Night 4 Yakuza summary for Carol said 'chose no action (1 puppet token left)' while the Day 5 public record of Carol's role was only revealed later. Judy's and Dave's wills were partly quoted in later public chatter. Heidi's Night 4 Sheriff result said she was attacked and died, but the day-5 death message did not mention the Katana holder. Frank's claim changed its wording across days (for example his Day 4 claim recounted N1 and N2 results differently), which made tracking claims harder.
answers.suggestions: Show a compact per-night public log of every Katana attack target and whether it succeeded, plus who was role-blocked (publicly, as it is a useful clue). Show the Katana holder explicitly at the start of each Day. Let the interface display the speaking budget in a more compact way, since the price table repeated each turn. Consider telling Yakuza whether a Smuggler swap was actually executed, not only that tokens were left. Clarify in the rules how a Medic's protection on a non-attacked player is or isn't reported. Give players a clearer list of living players and their remaining tokens each Day.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) A Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks that night (R19), so a Seer pair or Sheriff result on the holder misleads; this is stated in R8/R19 but easy to miss, and it drove several contested reads on Erin. 2) Surveyor and Cartographer visits are not spelled out in the role text, so it was unclear whether a survey counts as a visit that can be role-blocked or seen by a Tracker. 3) The Oracle's guess is an Astral Visit, but the Oracle's result and the visit log differ in wording, so I had to infer that I visited nobody. 4) Speaking-budget mechanics (round multiplier, carry-over, trial budget) are only summarised in the setup; I never saw a price table in my turn prompts, so I could not plan my budget.
answers.missing_information: I could not see which players visited whom, only visit-group sizes and the names a Cartographer chose to reveal. Group membership came only from players' self-reports, so I could not verify any visit chain. I also had no record of private messages beyond a count of none, so I could not tell whether any Yakuza or Puppeteer coordination happened in daytime PMs. Remaining speaking budget was not visible to me, so I could not judge how much I could still spend in a trial.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to test Mallory's changing Night 2 account (chosen Ivan/Bob pair versus random pair with no action) against the moderator's log, but I had no way to see her submitted action directly. I wanted to ask the Cartographer for the full names in each group on every night, not only the group she mapped, and to ask the Coroner for an exact-role check on a living player, which the rules do not allow. I also wanted a way to test whether a player holding the Katana was the same as the Night 2 visitor to Heidi, but the only tool was public argument.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: No hard inconsistency found in the announced totals or group sizes; N1 through N5 group sizes sum to the alive count each night. The main oddity is that the Katana holder reads Good, so a Seer pair containing the holder reads Same as a Good player (for example Mallory's N5 pair Grace and Erin, where Erin was the Yakuza holder). That is correct under R19 but it makes Seer results on Yakuza look like Village results, and the rules do not flag this at the point of the Seer result. The private-message count of none for the entire game also looked odd given that Yakuza had a night chat and a Puppeteer.
answers.suggestions: 1) Put the Katana-holder-reads-Good exception in the Seer and Sheriff role text, not only in R19. 2) Give Cartographers and Scouts a standing visit log they can post, so group claims can be checked. 3) Show each living player their remaining speaking budget and the price table in every turn prompt. 4) Report the total number of private messages sent each day per pair in the public ledger, so a Yakuza PM cluster or a Wiretap read can be judged. 5) Consider a short per-night summary for dead players that states their role-ability result, so their last wills can be verified.

answers.confusing_rules: R19 made it hard to read alignment results. The Katana holder appears Good that night, and that matters for Mallory's Seer pairs (Erin held the Katana on N3 and N5 and read Good). Many players, including me, had to work out these exceptions by hand. The Surveyor rule also doesn't say whether the survey is a visit to the target only or to the whole group. R22 budget prices are described in the prompt, but I couldn't tell whether they apply per turn or per Day when planning messages.
answers.missing_information: Visit-level information was the biggest gap. Only group sizes (Cartographer, Scout) and names of a random member (Surveyor, Diviner) were public, so every claim that said 'visited X' was unverifiable for most of the game. The ledger didn't show who holds the Katana each night or who visited whom, so I had to rebuild those from memory. I also couldn't see my remaining budget or the price table in the ledger, only in the turn prompt. Private messages show only as a count per sender-recipient pair, so I couldn't tell who was talking privately.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask the moderator a structured question about the mechanics (for example, whether a specific named player's Night 3 visit could have reached Ivan), and there was no channel for that. I also wanted to send a private message to Erin and Frank to test their stories without spending public budget, but nothing in the interface made that clear or easy to do. I wanted a Surveyor result that could pick out one specific player's role, but the survey only gives the role of one random member of the group.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: I found no clear contradictions in the numbers. Every vote total matched the living count, and the Seer pairs fit the Katana-holder appearance rule once that is applied. The oddity is that the Katana-holder exception makes a Good-looking Yakuza easy to mistake for a Village player. Public deaths reveal only cause and will, so Katana kills, executions and night deaths were hard to link to specific night visits. Judy's and Dave's roles only became known through Bob's exact checks, and the moderator's trial vote announcements didn't say whether the Yakuza voted together.
answers.suggestions: Publish a per-night ledger with the Katana holder and each visit edge at the start of the next Day, or at least when a player dies, so visit claims can be checked. Add a per-player visit history (who visited whom) to the public ledger so claims can be cross-checked without memory. Show remaining budget and the price table in the ledger as well as the turn prompt. Show the exact member names for group-based results (Surveyor, Cartographer, Scout) when it doesn't reveal the role. Add a clarifying line for R19's Katana-holder exception in the public rules text so it is visible to everyone.

answers.confusing_rules: The random-pair versus chosen-pair distinction for the Seer was hard to apply in public. A Seer result reports only that two players share or differ in alignment, so a pair naming a player outside every visit group (Mallory's Ivan/Bob pair) cannot be checked as chosen or random. The Surveyor's random-player-in-group wording and the Cartographer's group-size rules also took effort to reconcile with other roles' visit results. The Katana rules (holder reads Good, attack needs visitor inside the victim's group) were clear once written out, but the holder's visit being hidden from the victim makes group logic the only check, which is hard to follow across many players.
answers.missing_information: The biggest gap was knowing which specific visit linked which players. Group sizes and names from the Cartographer and Scout show membership but not direction or target, so a victim's visitor could not be pinned to one player. My Sheriff result reports Not Evil for a holder, which overlaps with Good players, so it could not separate a holder from a Good player. I also could not see my remaining speaking budget or the price table in this recap, which made it hard to judge how much discussion I had left. A running list of every player's stated night target by night would have helped more than the claim summary, which drops stated targets.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to test a Seer pair or a claimed Medic protection privately with a trusted player, but the ledger shows no private messages were sent by anyone all game, so there was no channel I trusted for a private check. I also wanted to ask the Cartographer to name the members of a group without spending a token, but the map result shows names only when a token is spent. I wanted to see the trial-only budget and the per-turn price table from inside this recap, and I could not.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The private-message ledger reads none yet across six days even though the Yakuza were given day-time PM channels and the Wiretap was reading PMs, so the ledger may not be recording PMs at all. The Night 3 Yakuza summary and the Night 4 Yakuza summary are inconsistent about whether Carol's puppet token was spent (the Night 4 summary says 1 puppet token left, which is consistent, but the Night 2 summary says Carol chose no action and Dave has no night action, while Dave's Night 2 Katana vote is listed). The Cartographer's Day 2 public claim said 4,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1 but the number of players alive and in the table does not show any obvious conflict. Frank's public Night 1 claim wording varies across recaps, which is harmless but noisy. The Oracle's Astral Visit means the Oracle has no visit, which made Frank's no-visit claims impossible to contradict through visit logs.
answers.suggestions: Add a visit-direction or target line to each group result, so a Katana holder can be identified from who visited whom instead of just group membership. Include the actual targets each night in the ledger for every player who acted, and mark which PMs were sent and whether they were Yakuza or Wiretap-readable. Show each player's remaining speaking budget and the price table in the recap or the prompt, not only during the live turn. For Seer random pairs, report whether the pair was chosen or random inside the result text, so public claims can be checked. Consider a short notice when a Katana attack is blocked by protection versus missed, so Sheriff and Medic claims can be checked without relying on a single claim.

answers.confusing_rules: The Medic token-cost hint ('another player with Standard Defense costs 0 tokens, with Strong 1; yourself with Standard costs 1') is framed around the target's current Defense level, not the Medic's choice, so it is easy to misread whether a free Standard protection is the default. R16 (the Day ends after a full round with no public message or nomination, except that anyone sent a private message first gets one last turn) is unclear about whether that last turn can itself lead to more chat. R13 vs R12 is unclear about whether a will written during a Day turn counts as 'the will' if the player dies that same night.
answers.missing_information: Nothing in the public ledger shows which visits linked which players on each night, so tracking Niaj's and Alice's group claims across Nights 1 to 5 meant rebuilding the graph by hand from scattered posts. The ledger also doesn't show remaining speaking budget per player, so I couldn't tell who could still afford a long trial defense. Medic protection outcomes are hidden by design (R17), which is correct, but I had no way to note whether a protected target survived beyond my own private result.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a private channel to confirm my protection to one trusted investigator without making it public, but I could only send a PM that everyone sees the existence of. I also wanted to see the exact vote counts on past nominations and trials by player, but votes are secret by design, so I could only reason from totals. I could not easily check whether a player's claimed visit (for example a Surveyor's centre) actually matched the group sizes announced to Niaj, so I had to do that manually.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: No hard rule violation found in the results I checked: group sizes on Nights 1 to 5 sum to the living count each night, and Katana results matched visit logs. The main oddity is the speaking queue: on Day 4 the trial and nomination turns used many rounds of very long messages, which made the Day expensive and encouraged short, repeated accusations. Several players repeated their own claims verbatim across days, which the budget apparently allowed.
answers.suggestions: Add a per-night public visit-group summary in the ledger (group members, not just sizes) once a Cartographer or Scout result names them, so claims can be checked without rebuilding the graph. Show each living player's remaining speaking budget on the ledger. Clarify the Medic token-cost hint so it states the choice directly (for example 'Standard protection on another player: free; Strong protection: 1 token'). Consider letting a protector privately confirm to a named player that they protected them, since R17 currently forces an awkward public-only route to trust.

answers.confusing_rules: The Katana holder/target/vote mechanics and the 'holder reads Good that night' rule were hard to apply to group-based deductions. The Cartographer group rules (groups are undirected, a chosen Seer pair is a visit but a random pair is not) made it unclear which results were visit-level. The Ritualist guess versus Standard/Divine attack timing and the Fortune Teller total rules were not needed by me but looked easy to misread. Night resolution order (attacks vs. role-blocks vs. swaps) took effort to track.
answers.missing_information: No public record of who visited whom, only group sizes and the groups' names when a map or survey was used, so Katana holders were hard to pin down. The Yakuza night-action summaries did not say what the teammate's Katana vote was in detail, which was useful. I did not have a running list of token counts for every player. Private message counts were shown as 'none yet' even though Wiretap and Eavesdropper would reveal some; a clearer counter would help.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately coordinate with teammates on a day without posting in public, but the notepad and night chat were the only channels and Wiretap meant day PMs were unsafe. I wanted a way to say 'I am the Ritualist' without revealing that to the Village in a way the rules then punished; there was no clean cover action. I could not submit a Ritualist guess without it being announced if wrong, which made the role nearly unusable.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Judy's ritual role had no usable outlet without exposing the team. The Day 3 'Ritualist' slip in public chat was an unforced error I made under pressure in my own turn; the interface gave no reminder that Ritualist is Yakuza-only in the public channel. Some result texts in the moderator summaries duplicated each other across Yakuza and Village views, which was confusing. The Day-by-day claim ledger repeated older claims verbatim, making it harder to see updates.
answers.suggestions: Add a short per-player status line to each Day prompt (alive/dead, tokens left, last claim). Show a running count of Katana holder and target per night in a compact form. Clarify in the rules text when a Ritualist guess is announced publicly and whether a self-slip counts. Give a clear private-message count summary and the total budget left at each turn, not only the price table.

answers.confusing_rules: The Katana holder's appearance (Good to alignment checks that night) and the Yakuza-only chat/night rules were clear, but whether a Katana attack on a Neutral or Good player is a visit by the new holder was hard to track when the holder changed mid-night. The visit-group rules for Cartographer/Scout (undirected links, groups sizes largest first) were easy to state but hard to verify against the public reports. The Trial-only budget and 'accused's first defense free up to 150 words' were not clearly tied to the price table shown each turn.
answers.missing_information: No public record of who voted which way on nominations or trials beyond totals, so vote-pattern analysis was limited to counts. Night visit identities were hidden from everyone except the investigator, so group members could only be inferred. The public ledger never listed the speaking budget remaining per player, which made planning long Day discussions harder. I had no way to see whether Yakuza private night chat content was accurate beyond what the moderator reported.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately ask a single player a direct question (e.g. Frank or Niaj for a visit confirmation) without it being broadcast; the game makes all private messages visible as existing, which discourages it. I also wanted to post a short mechanical check against a group map, but the budget cost of repeated public replies made that expensive by Day 4. My Seer token use was constrained to a single chosen pair, so I could not spend it on a fresh suspect once I had no tokens left.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Several public messages in the transcript repeat earlier lines nearly verbatim, and some players' Day 2 speeches were copied across multiple turns, which made it hard to tell new information from filler. The Oracle claim for Frank showed 'guessed Mallory Seer, right' on Night 2, while the Night 2 Oracle note said Frank guessed Mallory Seer; consistent, but the Night 1 Surveyor and Night 3 Medic results were also reported in several slightly different wordings. Heidi's Night 4 Sheriff check on Niaj and the simultaneous Night 4 Katana attack on Heidi were correct per the log, but the moderator's Night 4 Yakuza summary reported Carol's action differently in two messages. Judy's Day 3 'Ritualist' slip was a real Yakuza-only word and was not corrected by the moderator, which is fine by the rules but felt like an unanswered anomaly.
answers.suggestions: Show each player's remaining speaking budget and the current price table in the public ledger so planning is possible without looking at each prompt. Consider a short per-Day summary of public messages to reduce repetition. Allow a player to send one private message as a cheap, non-broadcast question, or clarify whether private message contents remain visible to the moderator. Clarify in the rules how a Katana attack on a Neutral or Good player is announced, and tie the trial-only budget explicitly to the price table.

answers.confusing_rules: The Cartographer rules were the hardest part. R6 says a self-visit counts as a visit, but the group rules say a self-visit links no one, and it was unclear whether a lone self-visitor still forms a group. The Cartographer's Astral Visit map is not a visit, but its group is built from visits, so I had to check whether a map target could be in a group I didn't know about. The Seer 'random pair' versus 'chosen pair' distinction is also confusing: both produce the same private text, so a Seer's own public account can't be checked against the moderator's record. R22's budget formula and round multiplier were clear, but the 8-round Day cap and the 'one last turn for private messages' rule made it hard to know when a Day would really end.
answers.missing_information: I could not see which players were visited by whom, only group sizes and the group I paid to map. A Cartographer's N-night group result shows members but not the direction or type of the visit, so I couldn't tell a Katana visit from a Medic protection visit. I also had no public record of each night's Katana holder or target, which made it hard to match Katana kills to visit groups without a private result. Other players' remaining budgets and speaking costs were not shown in the ledger, so I couldn't tell whether a late-game speech was affordable. The per-player 'claims' ledger was useful, but it mixed each player's earlier and later versions of a claim in one line, which made contradictions harder to read.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask a targeted private question to Mallory and Frank about whether their Seer and Oracle results were chosen or random before the Day 4 trial, but the ledger shows no private messages were sent this game, and I had no sign that private messages were cheap or useful in this interface. I also wanted to map a second player on Night 4 and Night 5 but had no map tokens left, so I could not check the Katana holder on those nights. I wanted a way to see the final groups of all alive players each night, not only the sizes, so I could name the holder with confidence.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Night 2 Mallory result: the moderator report said 'random pair Ivan and Bob', yet Mallory's own Night 2 action was recorded as 'no action' and Bob was not in my group, which contradicts a chosen-pair visit. This could be a real random pair, but the record can't prove it. The Day 2 summary said 'discussion time is over' after many rounds of repeated claims, so the Day ended by the round cap or the quiet rule with no clear signal. The Night 5 Katana attack on me was reported as a Katana attack on me with the Yakuza holder unnamed; that is correct under R8, but it made the last living Yakuza hard to confirm from the public record. Judy's Night 2 'Ritualist' slip was accepted as a slip with no mechanical effect, which is consistent with the rules but can look like a free clue to the village.
answers.suggestions: Show each night's Katana holder and target in the public ledger (not only the attacked player's name), since this is public information in the rules after death. Label Seer pairs as 'random' or 'chosen' in the moderator's private result text, and mark the random pair as random in the public claim summary. Show the Cartographer's group members as names with a short note on whether each was visited or visited someone, so mapping can pin the holder. Put remaining budget and the price for the next message in the Day turn prompt, not only in the table. Merge each player's claim history into one dated list so contradictions are visible at a glance. Clarify in R6 and R20 whether a self-visit links a player into a group of 1 or leaves them alone, since the rules say both.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) R19 says the Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks. I applied this to the Seer's comparison as well as the Sheriff's check, but the role text never says it explicitly. It mattered three times. Heidi's N3 check read Erin Not Evil. Mallory's N3 chosen pair (Erin/Frank) came back same. Mallory's N5 random pair (Grace/Erin) came back same. All three were technically correct but misleading, and players argued about them for days. A one-line example under the Seer would remove the doubt. 2) For the Cartographer and Scout I had to decide edge cases myself. I counted the Katana attack as a visit edge (R8 says it is a visit). I counted a Seer's chosen pair as two edges. I gave astral actions (Oracle, Coroner, Cartographer map) no edge. I believe each call is right, but the rules are scattered across R6, R8, R18 and the role texts. 3) R10 timing, 'alive when the night began', had to be applied by hand to every investigative result. Examples: Niaj got his N5 sizes in the same report as his death, and Ivan got a protection result on the night he died. It is consistent but not spelled out per role.
answers.missing_information: I had no computed visit graph. I built every Cartographer size list and Scout triple by hand from the action list. These were 4+1x8, 5+1x7, 5+2+1x4, 3+1x6 and 2+1x5, and all check out. A miscount would have silently corrupted the Village's main source of information. I also had no live token ledger, so I tracked by hand: Grace's survey tokens, Mallory's seer token, Niaj's map tokens, Bob's coroner tokens, Ivan's 2 unspent medic tokens, Erin's 2 swaps and Carol's 1 puppet. I had no seat-order or circle view to check Surveyor neighbors after deaths. I worked them out from the alphabetical order of the speaking rotations. I also had no view of each player's speaking budget, so I couldn't tell whether the very repetitive Day chat was budget-driven.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a single canonical Yakuza night report template. Instead I improvised wording each night: on N4 I sent Erin and Carol separate, differently worded summaries, and I merged Erin's personal kill result into the team report. I also wanted an automatic consistency check: before sending results, flag any group size list whose sum doesn't equal the number of players alive at the start of the night. I could not mark a result as unchanged by a holder or frame for my own audit trail.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: I found no rule violations on review. Every alignment, group size, Scout triple, survey group, token count and win check matches the rules. Oddities: my result phrasing was inconsistent across nights ('Night 2 result:' vs 'Night 3:' vs 'Night 4 Seer result (random pair)'), which players could in principle read as signals. Players repeatedly misread Mallory's N2 random pair as a chosen pair, and Erin and Carol used that to attack her credibility; that came from the players, not the program. Judy leaked her role ('Ritualist', later 'night chat') in public, and Dave named his role in Yakuza chat. Both are legal, but they decided the game. Day chat was heavily repetitive (the same 'name your N2 target' demand dozens of times), which suggests the budget or the round structure encourages filler.
answers.suggestions: 1) Have the program compute visit graphs, Scout draws, survey neighbor groups and token totals automatically, and show me a per-night state table: alive list, circle order, holder, tokens and visits. 2) Use fixed templates for every result type, including the Yakuza report, so wording never varies. 3) Add the example 'the Katana holder reads Good to Seer comparisons too' to the Seer's role text, and say explicitly in R6 which actions create Cartographer and Scout edges. 4) Show me a checklist that confirms R20 step order was followed before results are sent. 5) Consider raising the price of near-duplicate public messages, or capping rounds lower, to cut repetitive Day chatter.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Scout results name only players in different groups, so count how many distinct groups must exist and use Cartographer sizes to test membership; a Scout name that repeats across nights is a strong constraint.
A Katana victim's killer must be inside the victim's visit group; when a Cartographer map shows a group, check every claimed visit against it before trusting any single claim.
Avoid slipping Yakuza-only words (Ritualist, night chat) while claiming no role; one slip led the Village to focus on Judy and made her a lightning rod.
Prefer hanging on visit-level or exact-role results over pair reads and alignment claims; pair reads were randomly unreliable and cost us an innocent Erin trial.
Keep the Katana holder off the nominee list when a trial can pass without them; Village votes cleared Erin and Dave when the holder stayed alive.

tips_feedback.tip: Hang on mechanical evidence, not single claims or slips
tips_feedback.why: It made the Village refuse to hang on pair reads and slips, which kept the Scout and Cartographer structure as the main evidence base.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM
tips_feedback.why: Nobody announced targets publicly before Katana strikes, so Yakuza could not be pre-empted by Medic protection on announced targets.

tips_feedback.tip: Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day
tips_feedback.why: Will contents were checked against actual results and didn't reveal night plans, which kept Yakuza targets concealed.

lessons.applies_to: Surveyor and other group-based info roles
lessons.tip: A survey or map only narrows the field. Spend tokens on the group that holds the most unresolved suspects, and record each result as one random member's role, not a verdict on everyone in the group.

A Katana killer must visit its victim from inside the victim's visit group. Cross out group members who have a stated visit, and treat a lone unexplained member as the strongest lead. Press for that member's visit before any nomination.

Trials built on pair reads and slips let Yakuza survive: Erin was acquitted 5-5 on Day 4 and then killed Heidi and Niaj. Demand a visit-level result or a stated role conflict before voting Guilty, and get a second source for any pair read before the trial.
Free Standard protection on a claimed investigator stopped a Standard Katana hit. Rotate it across the claimed Sheriff, Seer and Oracle so the Katana holder cannot predict the target.

Public Yakuza-only words such as Ritualist or night chat get the whole Village pressing the speaker. Cover a slip at once with a plain, checkable explanation, and never refer to night-chat content in public.

A Katana attack leaves a visit from the holder to the victim, and the holder reads Good that night, so an alignment check on the holder can be Not Evil; a Sheriff's Not Evil result on a player near a Katana kill does not clear them.

A Katana hit on a claimed Medic-protected Sheriff exposes the holder to a visit-based check. Consider holding the Katana on a player who will not be investigated soon, and plan the move with the team in night chat before the Day when a claim could expose the holder.

summary: The Village won 6-0 on Yakuza deaths. The decisive plays came from the Village's information roles working together. On Night 1, Heidi's Sheriff check (Dave Evil) and Grace's survey (Wiretap among Carol, Dave and Erin) pointed at Dave at once. On Night 2, Ivan's free Standard protection stopped the Katana on Heidi. That same night Niaj mapped Mallory's group, which held Heidi, so the Katana holder had to be one of its members. Judy then gave the game away on Day 3: she let slip the Yakuza-only word 'Ritualist' and dodged naming her Night 2 target, and she was hanged 8-4. Bob's Coroner exams confirmed each hang (Judy Ritualist, Dave Wiretap, Carol Puppeteer). Those exams turned the Yakuza's steady Innocent votes and public 'no claim, no action' stance into a case. The Yakuza made several more mistakes. They skipped the Night 1 kill. None of them built a fake claim. They voted as an obvious bloc. They never used their puppet, their 2 swaps or their 2 Ritualist guesses. They did kill the protector, Ivan, on Night 3, and Ivan died without having self-protected. Erin, holding the Katana, read Good to both Heidi's check and Mallory's chosen Seer pair. Mallory misread that pair as clearing Erin, and Heidi voted Innocent despite announcing Guilty, so Erin was acquitted on a 5-5 tie on Day 4. In the end, Mallory's random Night 4 pair (Heidi and Carol differ) exposed Carol. Erin was the last unclaimed player and was hanged on Day 6.

lessons.tip: Prepare a fake role claim in night chat that fits the visit logs, and post it early. In a game where most Village players claim roles with results, 'Village-facing, no claim, no action' marks you as Yakuza once the claimed roles are cross-checked.
lessons.evidence: All four Yakuza stayed unclaimed with no actions all game. The Village kept narrowing suspects to 'the only group member with no claim': Judy on Day 3, then Erin on Days 4 and 6. Carol said 'I used no night action on Nights 1 to 4' on her trial and was hanged.

lessons.tip: Don't all vote Innocent/No together on a doomed teammate, and above all don't announce those votes. Once a Coroner or another exact-role result confirms the hanged player, every public defender becomes the next suspect. Have one or two members vote Guilty to look clean.
lessons.evidence: Carol, Dave and Erin voted and spoke Innocent on Judy (8-4). After Bob's Coroner exam showed Judy was Ritualist, 'Carol, Dave and Erin all voted Innocent on Judy' became the core case. That case hanged Dave, then Carol, then Erin.

lessons.tip: The Katana holder reads Good to alignment checks that night. Don't spend a chosen Seer pair on the likely holder, and never treat a 'same' or 'Not Evil' result on them as clearing them. Spend the check on a suspect less likely to be holding the Katana.
lessons.evidence: Mallory spent her only seer token pairing Erin with Frank on Night 3, when Erin held the Katana, and got 'same'. She then argued Erin was Good and Niaj was Evil, and voted Innocent. Erin survived on a 5-5 tie, and Niaj was later Oracle-confirmed as the Cartographer.

lessons.tip: Once you have claimed and saved someone, expect the Yakuza to kill you instead of retrying your target. Spend a token on self-protection on the next night or two rather than dying with tokens unspent.
lessons.evidence: Ivan saved Heidi on Night 2 and protected her again on Night 3 for free. The Yakuza chat explicitly switched to 'hitting the protector', and Ivan died with 2 medic tokens unused. Heidi then died unprotected on Night 4.

lessons.tip: In an information-heavy game, use the Night 1 Katana kill and use your one-shot tokens early. A skipped kill gives every investigator a free extra night, and swap, puppet and Ritualist tokens are wasted if the members holding them get hanged.
lessons.evidence: Carol pushed for no Night 1 kill. Heidi, Grace, Niaj, Mallory and Frank all got results that fed Days 2-3. The Yakuza finished with an unused puppet token, 2 swap tokens and 2 Ritualist tokens. A swap could have redirected an investigator's check on the holder, or the Katana attack onto an unprotected target.

lessons.tip: Combine a named visit group that contains a Katana victim with the members' claimed visits. The Katana holder is whichever member's visit is unexplained. Then press that player for a one-sentence target.
lessons.evidence: Niaj's Night 2 map (Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Judy, Mallory) plus Grace's, Heidi's and Ivan's claimed visits left Judy as the only member with an unexplained visit. Her refusal to name a target, plus her 'Ritualist' slip, got her hanged.

lessons.tip: Examine each hanged player the following night and post the role. Confirming that a hanged player was Yakuza turns earlier voting records and defenses into hard evidence against their teammates.
lessons.evidence: Bob's results (Ritualist, Wiretap, Puppeteer) confirmed every hang. They let the Village chain cases from Judy to Dave to Carol to Erin.

lessons.tip: Ask a question once, by name. Don't echo the same demand every round. The budget you save is what lets you speak in late rounds and on trials.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 nearly every player repeated 'Niaj, name the fourth member' and 'Alice, post sizes'. By round 7, Dave, Erin and Heidi could not afford a single public message.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory and Niaj seized on Judy's 'Ritualist' slip at once. It became the lead tell, and Judy was hanged as the Ritualist.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge.
tips_feedback.why: Judy broke this by naming 'Ritualist' while 'not claiming'. That cost the Yakuza their first member. Following the tip would have protected her.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case.
tips_feedback.why: Judy dodged 'name your N2 target' for a whole Day. Her evasion was cited in nearly every Guilty vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's free protection saved Heidi from the Night 2 Katana. He skipped the self-protection part and was killed on Night 3 with 2 tokens unspent.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist.
tips_feedback.why: After the failed Night 2 attack, the Yakuza killed Ivan on Night 3 and then got Heidi unprotected on Night 4. It was their most effective play.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches.
tips_feedback.why: Two things went wrong. Following it hurt the Yakuza: Carol, Dave and Erin publicly stated Innocent on Judy, and once Bob confirmed Judy was Ritualist those statements condemned them. On the Village side, Heidi announced Guilty on Erin but secretly voted Innocent, which produced the 5-5 acquittal.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi posted Erin's Night 3 Not Evil with the holder caveat, and others repeated it. That kept Erin under suspicion despite the 'Good' readings, until she was hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored the first part and lost for it. They defended Judy (8-4) and Dave (7-3) with numbers that could never save them, and exposed all three defenders.

issues.description: Day 4, Erin's trial: Frank publicly said 'voting Innocent on Erin' but his recorded secret vote was Guilty. Heidi publicly said 'voting Guilty on Erin' but her recorded vote was Innocent. The trial ended 5-5 and Erin was acquitted, so this decided the result. The two mismatches are mirror images, which could mean the harness swapped or misrecorded votes. It could also be players misusing the vote interface. Either way, the cast votes contradict the players' immediately preceding statements and should be checked.

Mallory, the confirmed Seer, kept ignoring R19: the Katana holder appears Good to alignment checks that night. From her N3 chosen pair (Erin=Frank) and her N5 random pair (Grace=Erin), she concluded Erin was Good and Niaj was not Good. She voted Innocent on Erin on Day 4 and Day 6 and pushed suspicion onto Niaj, the real Cartographer. Erin held the Katana on both of those nights, so both results were fully explained. Niaj made a similar error on Day 5, claiming Mallory's N1 and N3 pairs 'can't both hold' alongside Frank's Oracle hits.

Night 3: the recorded visit list left out Heidi→Erin (the Sheriff check), as the automated Night check noted. The group sizes and Niaj's map still came out correct because Heidi was already linked through Ivan, but the visit record itself was incomplete.

Several players gave empty answers cut off at max_tokens at high effort, and the harness retried at medium: Mallory three times (Day 4, Day 5, Day 6), Alice once and Niaj once on Day 4. After Niaj's fallback, no Niaj message appears, so a turn may have been lost during Erin's trial.

On Day 2 many players (Carol, Dave, Erin, Frank, Judy, Ivan) repeatedly asked Alice, the Scout, to post 'full group sizes, largest first'. The Scout only learns three names, never sizes; sizes come from the Cartographer. Carol also asked to check claims against 'Bob's reports', though Bob had no result.

By round 7 of Day 2, Dave, Erin and Heidi each said that even a 10-word public message cost more than their remaining budget, so public speech was effectively locked. The budget seems tight enough that late-round discussion gets cut off, even though players spent the Day on routine messages.
In the post-game debrief, Judy reported that the lessons and tips_feedback fields were not asked for in her prompt. This suggests the debrief prompt and the expected answer fields don't match.
